question.text:
The equations $x^{2}+x+a=0 \quad$ and
$x^{2}+a x+1=0$ have a common real root

solution.text:
Let \(\alpha\) be the common roots
\(\begin{array}{l}
\therefore \alpha^{2}+\alpha+a=0 \ldots \text { (i) } \\
\text { and } \alpha^{2}+a \alpha+1=0 \ldots \text { (ii) } \\
\frac{\alpha^{2}}{1-a^{2}}=\frac{\alpha}{a-1}=\frac{1}{a-1}[a \neq 1]
\end{array}\)
Eliminating \(\alpha\), we get
\(\begin{array}{l}
(a-1)^{2}=\left(1-a^{2}\right)(a-1) \\
\Rightarrow a-1)=1-a^{2} \\
\Rightarrow a^{2}+a-2=0 \\
\Rightarrow a^{2}+2 a-a-2=0 \\
\Rightarrow a(a+2)-1(a+2)=0 \\
\Rightarrow(a+2)(a-1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow a=-2 \cdot[\because a \neq 1]
\end{array}\)
